Here is the comparison between the official Teams integration roadmap and informal sales or Slack claims, based solely on the supplied evidence.

The official roadmap [NL-014#NL-014-S07] states the Microsoft Teams integration is under "Active Design and Planning" with a release target of Q4 2026 (v2.11.0, November release). Its security architecture is to use Azure Active Directory tokens for user verification and role-based permission enforcement, with a restricted pilot beginning in October 2026 for selected financial and healthcare accounts [NL-014#NL-014-S07].

In contrast, informal sales claims made by Marcus Reed state the integration is "basically right around the corner," has a "working connector" almost ready for "general release," and can be included in a July pilot [NL-023#NL-023-S04]. He also proposed targeting a July or August pilot to secure renewals and close prospects [NL-027#NL-027-S02], and suggested packaging the existing proof-of-concept as an "alpha" for a client threatening to churn [NL-027#NL-027-S04].

These claims are directly contradicted by internal technical and management evidence. Chloe (engineering) confirms the existing demo is a "toy" with zero tenant isolation, zero permission mapping, zero SSO, and zero formatting/citation links [NL-027#NL-027-S03]. Leon (CTO) explicitly states the integration is NOT "right around the corner" and is slated for design in Q4 2026 [NL-027#NL-027-S03]. Sofia (Product) declares the roadmap remains the source of truth [NL-027#NL-027-S04], and Raj (Infra) rejects any one-off custom builds [NL-027#NL-027-S04]. The CTO and Product lead further refuse to shift resources to accelerate the timeline, keeping it in design for Q4 and development for early 2027 [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

The official sales playbook also clarifies that roadmap dates are targets, not guarantees, and specifies the Teams integration is in the planning and design phase for Q4 2026 [NL-009#NL-009-S08]. Management is actively enforcing training to prevent sales reps from overclaiming integration readiness [NL-016#NL-016-S05]. Ultimately, the sales claims of near-completion are informal overclaims that conflict with the official Q4 2026 roadmap and the engineering reality of a non-secure, pre-proof-of-concept state.
